chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
How excellent is the humility of the rich towards the poor, seeking what is with Allah! And better than that is the haughtiness of the poor towards the rich, relying on Allah.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the humility of the rich and the haughtiness of the poor in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) contrasts the active humility of the wealthy, who lower themselves to the poor to seek divine reward, with the dignified self-assurance of the poor, whose 'haughtiness' stems from complete reliance on Allah. This dichotomy highlights two distinct spiritual states: the wealthy must actively cultivate *tawadu'* (humility) to avoid arrogance, while the poor, trusting in divine provision, maintain a noble dignity that is not mere pride but a reflection of their spiritual independence. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on inner intention (*niyyah*) and the balance between social interaction and spiritual trust (*tawakkul*).
